svg.aria-label: Five stations in a row, from the database on the left to the reader on the right: Postgres, the Node application, the Nginx proxy, a CDN which was not tested, and the reader. Below the row, two nested bars show how much work each cache placement removes. A one-second cache inside the Node process spans the database box only: it skips the database, cuts about one hundred queries a second, and raises the ceiling from two thousand five hundred to four thousand concurrent users. The same one-second rule moved one hop out into Nginx spans both the database and the application: it skips both and raises the ceiling to five thousand two hundred and fifty. The nesting is the point, because each hop toward the reader removes strictly more work per request. A closing caption notes 2.1 times the users on the same machine with no change to the bill, and that the price is staleness bounded at one second, which is a product decision rather than a technical one.

svg.text: MOVE THE WORK CLOSER TO THE READER
